issues.description: Returning nil result after failed CAS breaks caller contract and will crash callers expecting a non-nil *result
issues.detail: In the new CAS-failure branch, `return nil` is propagated as `output` from `run`. Callers and the deferred logic that invoke `output.done`, `output.Fatal`, or store/forward this result will dereference nil. Most call sites of `task.run` assume a non-nil *result; returning nil here just relocates the original NPE rather than fixing it.

issues.description: Cycle check skipped on the late-arrival waiter path, allowing undetected cycles to deadlock
issues.detail: Previously `waitUntilDone` was called after cycle detection on the pending branch. Now when the CAS fails (another goroutine became leader), the code calls `waitUntilDone` directly with no `checkCycle` call. A caller already on the path that arrives after leader assignment will wait indefinitely on `output.done` instead of returning ErrCycle.

issues.description: Comment 'Leader panicked but we did see a result' appears inverted and misleading
issues.detail: The comment says 'we did see a result' but the code path is entered precisely when `t.result.Load()` returned nil, i.e., we did NOT see a result. Likely intended 'did not see'. This will confuse future readers debugging the same race.

issues.description: Race window between CompareAndSwap failure and reload is not fully reasoned about
issues.detail: Between `CompareAndSwap(nil, output)` failing and `t.result.Load()` returning nil, the leader must have stored then cleared the result. Without a memory-ordering note or test exercising this interleaving, future refactors may break the invariant. Add a comment explaining the panic-recovery sequence in the leader path that allows result to become nil again.

issues.description: Shadowed variable `output` in CAS-failure branch reduces readability and risks future bugs
issues.detail: The block declares `output := t.result.Load()` which shadows the named return `output` from `run`. The function already has `output *result` as a return value initialized to the CAS candidate. Shadowing here makes it easy to misread which `output` is used and complicates the existing deferred logic if any is added later.

issues.description: No regression test added for the documented race condition
issues.detail: The PR description identifies a specific race (leader panic clears `t.result` while waiters select on `t.result.Load().done`). Without a test that reproduces the panic-then-waiter sequence (e.g., using a query that panics with concurrent waiters), the fix can silently regress. Recommend a targeted test with `-race` and `GOMAXPROCS>1`.

review.summary: The PR refactors cycle detection into a helper and addresses a real nil-deref race on `t.result.Load().done`, but the chosen fix introduces two serious problems. First, returning a bare `nil` from `run` when the leader's result has been cleared likely just moves the NPE to the caller, which expects a non-nil *result. Second, the CAS-failure path no longer runs `checkCycle`, so a late-arriving caller already on the cycle path will block on `output.done` instead of returning ErrCycle. The comment on the new branch also appears inverted ("did see" vs "did not see"). A regression test that reproduces the panicking-leader race under `-race` would substantially de-risk this change.
